title: Where it grows
subtitle: The Veneto
objectives: Explain the role of volcanic soils

steps.title: Soave
steps.body: Garganega grows mainly in the Veneto, east of Verona, around Soave. Soave DOC must be at least 70% Garganega, with Trebbiano di Soave or Chardonnay. Soave Classico, in the hills around Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone, is the historic core. Gambellara, next door, also uses it.

steps.title: Volcanic hills
steps.body: Soave Classico's hills have volcanic basalt soils, dark and mineral-rich, as well as limestone. Volcanic soils give wines with more structure, saline notes and ageing potential. Vineyards are traditionally trained on pergolas, called pergola veronese, which shade the fruit. Flat land below makes simpler Soave.

steps.explanation: Soave's hills give its best wines.

steps.title: Crus
steps.body: Since 2019, Soave recognises 33 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, named sub-areas, like Foscarino, Calvarino and Monte Fiorentine. These help consumers find the best sites. Producers like Pieropan and Inama helped show Soave's potential.

steps.prompt: What soils give Soave Classico its structure?
steps.explanation: Basalt and limestone give mineral, structured wines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Garganega grows around Soave, east of Verona
Soave Classico's volcanic hills give its best wines
